study.question: Does equal occupied-match-group mass make the strongest grouped representation and target-query readout complementary, or do uniform extra feature paths explain the existing hybrid gain?
study.hypothesis: OBSERVATIONS: Baseline static/pooled/DIN AUCs are 0.6050036145/0.6102261137/0.6133619861. Frozen paired_match is 0.6191087654 (Logloss 0.1958610589, wall 572.30s, inference 16.20s); source target_separate is 0.6153351064. The four successful hybrid trajectories are target-separate 0.6198705488, context-separate 0.6200552833, target-joint 0.6199300812, context-joint 0.6198865703. Thus target queries lose 0.0001847345 with separate reads, but gain 0.0000435109 with consensus reads: no consistent conditioning or separation mechanism support. All four have worse Logloss than paired_match (0.1959856072/0.1960083923/0.1958674091/0.1960128929) and wall costs 792.34/803.12/797.42/803.90s. The incumbent first-512 diagnostic reports 118.115 mean visible events and about 2.025 occupied groups. The ancestor paired_match diagnostics report group count means 107.867 neither, 7.869 category-only, 1.430 brand-only, 0.949 both; these are candidate-supplied small-sample diagnostics, not population proof. Existing empty/1-16-history slices also lose AUC versus paired_match; their low positive counts and altered training preclude a causal subgroup claim. No failed empirical trials are supplied; search for failure/abandoned trajectories returned no scoped-memory hits. No failed execution is reclassified as counterevidence. PROVISIONAL MECHANISM: Global field softmax may use its mass budget primarily on abundant unrelated events or spend target conditioning on between-group allocation already represented by exact match groups. Fixing equal total mass per occupied group may let target queries select useful residual information within groups. Dominance of count does not prove dominance of learned weights; new mass diagnostics can falsify this account. ALTERNATIVE: The existing gain may be explained by redundant input reparameterization or 2048 added classifier weights; uniform summaries test that directly. The prior null target contrast is retained, not erased. Novelty and predictive utility of the new normalization are unverified.

study.proposed_difference: For occupied match groups G_g and K occupied groups, use field weights w_fi = softmax_{j in G_g}(s_fj)/K for i in G_g, zero for masked events. Scores, key/value definitions and full original feature path are unchanged. Category and brand normalize separately; their common action/recency value uses the mean of field weights, as in the ancestor. balanced_target uses current-ad queries; balanced_context replaces only queries with history means; balanced_uniform zero-scales score tensors while keeping their graph; global_uniform selects zero-score global softmax. All cells compute both global and grouped weights and combine them with fixed 0/1 coefficients, retaining identical module allocation; uniform scorer gradients are identically zero by design and are not called active capacity. The two uniform summaries are determined by existing group means/sizes; any gain there is consistent with reparameterization/capacity effects. This is a controlled local normalization intervention, not a verified new architecture or a claim of world-first priority.
predictions: Implementation checks: each balanced field assigns mass 1/K to every occupied group; masked and empty group mass is zero; whole field mass is one for nonempty histories and zero otherwise. Within-group constant score shifts cannot change balanced weights.

Implementation checks: original group features and histograms stay unchanged. With one valid event every read equals its event vector; masked padding, event order and zero-length histories preserve valid features/logits up to floating-point reduction error. Norm matching preserves reference norm except the declared safe fallback.

Discriminating prediction: if global group-mass competition blocks target residual selection, balanced_target should exceed balanced_context AND balanced_uniform on full-population validation AUC, with a better target-context difference than the existing global difference of -0.0001847345041644. Improvements over both source bests and the incumbent are separate utility requirements.

If balancing alone explains gains, balanced_uniform should capture them and target-conditioning remains unsupported. If extra feature paths explain the old gain, global_uniform should match the learned global references despite carrying no new information beyond the original group representation.

Record existing predeclared host slices (empty, 1-16, 17-64, >64 events; fixed hours/action presence/train-frequency groups; category match) with sample/positive/negative counts. Empty-history and 1-16 slices are low-support diagnostics. No mechanistic claim follows from seed-42 exploratory slices. New fixed-first-512 mass diagnostics are descriptive only and are not used to select or tune thresholds.

Use host AUC as primary, unweighted Logloss independently as secondary; report parameters/effective scorer status, wall/train/allocated GPU seconds when exposed, peak memory, examples processed when exposed, throughput and batch p50/p95. Missing cost metrics stay unavailable rather than being inferred. No equal-compute win is predicted from parameter equality.
falsifiers: A balanced group-mass error, nonzero masked/empty features, nonfinite logit, broken supplied mask or parameter-shape mismatch is an implementation failure; retain its charged receipt and repair before scientific comparison.
If the existing global retrieval already gives balanced masses or balanced normalization does not improve a learned cell, the proposed global-mass limitation is unsupported in this implementation.

balanced_target <= balanced_context leaves target-query complementarity unsupported even if both beat the incumbent. balanced_target <= balanced_uniform leaves learned target-conditioned within-group selection unsupported.

A hybrid unable to exceed g1-r0006-paired_match, g2-r0001-target_separate and g3-r0006-hybrid_context_separate does not establish incremental utility; better AUC with worse Logloss is a documented tradeoff.

Gains matched by global_uniform are consistent with added-path reparameterization rather than attention-derived information. One seed or a small fixed diagnostic sample cannot establish or refute a general mechanism.

If equal mass amplifies rare-group noise, hurts sparse-history slices, exceeds the fixed per-trial cap or loses on measured quality-cost comparison, do not claim an efficient improvement. An unsuccessful implementation is retained and may motivate a later admissible partial-balancing contrast, not a retroactive change to this proposal.
alternative_explanations: The complete match-group/count/histogram representation already contains the useful target association; additional target queries are redundant.
Global attention already selects rare matching events despite count imbalance; equal occupied mass can suppress useful target-driven between-group allocation.
Uniform extra features improve optimization or effective classifier parameterization without adding information; allocated scorer counts conceal differing effective trainability.
Group uniform balancing can dominate learned residual selection; sparse/rare groups may increase variance and global-norm matching may amplify weak or noisy summaries.

Seed/checkpoint variation, adaptive validation selection and interactions with learned shared embeddings may explain small AUC differences. AUC/Logloss disagreement and tiny sparse-history slices can mislead.
Original cached external studies have different labels, histories, splits and optimizers. Their attribution and transfer are unverified; no external result substitutes for a local controlled outcome.
